editorial.notes: The heading printed over a reading from a book named by its title. LÉCTIO is the nominative of a heading: no verb is expressed or understood. LIBRI is the genitive of liber (book), and the second genitive is the title of the book. The edition prints this heading over lessons from Wisdom, Proverbs, Ecclesiasticus and the Song of Songs; the explanation of SAPIÉNTIÆ says so.

source.method: The Latin follows the Benziger Brothers 1962 editio iuxta typicam, which prints this heading over the Epistle on printed p. 526 (IA leaf n607 / PDF p. 608) and over the 9 further readings named in the witness header; it is compared with the heading line of the pinned Divinum Officium file that the reading's own digital witness binds. Source review remains pending.
